guide.liveNote: These come from the game's current rules.

run.title: How a run goes
run.summary: Build a ship, take a mission, fly it, read what happened, repair and go again.
run.keywords: start begin loop basics tutorial first steps beginner

build.title: Build
build.text: Assemble the ship on My Ship from the parts you own: drag them onto the grid, or press Auto layout. Parts must touch, and their ports must line up (see Ports and connectors).

plan.title: Plan
plan.text: Pick a mission on Missions. Each row shows the trip's time and fuel for your ship and what the mission asks of it. Your ship can take a mission only when every requirement is met.

fly.title: Fly
fly.text: Dispatch the ship and it flies on the server's clock, so you can close the game and come back. Fights and mishaps on the way are decided by your ship's numbers and some luck.

read.title: Read and repeat
read.text: When the ship lands you get a report: the verdict, the pay, what the trip wore down and anything you found. Then repair, refuel, upgrade, and go again.

parts.title: Parts and the ship sheet
parts.summary: What each kind of part does, and what the numbers on the ship sheet mean.
parts.keywords: engine chemical ion thruster tank fuel battery reactor solar panel weapon cannon defense shield armor hull frame cargo hold sensor bridge utility life support sheet stats firepower mobility range energy structure

sheet.title: The ship sheet
sheet.text: Firepower is how hard you hit. Armor and shield are the pools a fight starts with. Cargo is the space for loads and ore. Mobility is how fast the ship flies. Range is the route distance a full tank covers. Condition is the average health of the parts. Energy is what your parts generate minus what they use while cruising. Structure is how much of the ship's structure budget the parts use. The budget comes from the bridge: a bigger bridge carries more.

engines.title: Engines
engines.text: Chemical engines push hard and burn fuel. Ion engines burn no fuel but need electric power from batteries or solar panels and push more gently. The engine tuning panel on My Ship lets you run chemical engines up to {{chemMax}} times and ion engines up to {{ionMax}} times their normal output, at the price of extra wear. The orange triangle on an engine marks its exhaust: keep that side free.

tanks.title: Fuel tanks
tanks.text: Tanks hold the fuel that chemical engines burn. The range on the ship sheet tells you how far a full tank takes you. A ship with only ion engines needs no tank at all.

power.title: Batteries, solar panels and reactors
power.text: Solar panels and reactors generate energy; many parts use it. Cruising energy should not be negative. Batteries store energy and cover the extra draw in a fight; the sheet says how many rounds they last.

weapons.title: Weapons
weapons.text: Weapons add firepower. Like engines they have a facing (the orange triangle marks the muzzle) and need their ports connected to work.

defense.title: Shield and armor
defense.text: In a fight damage meets the shield first; the shield recovers {{shieldRegen}} points at the start of each round. Then the armor: it cuts every hit by {{armorCut}} per point of armor rating and soaks the rest as a pool of {{armorPool}} points per rating point. What gets through hurts the hull and the parts.

cargo.title: Cargo and spare parts
cargo.text: Cargo space holds what a mission loads and the ore you dig. Loose spare parts do not use cargo: they ride in {{spareSlots}} separate slots, one slot per part.

sensors.title: Sensors
sensors.text: Sensors help you spot an ambush before it starts and help you slip away from a fight.

utility.title: Hull frames and utility parts
utility.text: Hull frames hold the ship together and give it body; life support and pumps keep other systems working. A part that is not connected to the rest counts for nothing.

bridge.title: The bridge
bridge.text: No bridge, no flight. The bridge's rarity is your bridge level: it decides how rare the parts in the shops get and how well missions pay. You can make it bigger or smaller from the Upgrade tab at a port.

ports.title: Ports and connectors
ports.summary: The dots on the edges of parts: what they mean and how to fix a red one.
ports.keywords: connector connection port green red blue incorrect available disconnected shape kind

colors.title: Reading the colours
colors.text: Green: connected, the two parts talk to each other. Red: incorrect, a port meets a port of a different kind or points at nothing it can use. Blue: available, an open port with nothing next to it (that is fine).

kinds.title: Kinds of connector
kinds.text: A kind is drawn by how many dots sit on the edge. Only matching kinds connect. Rotating a part turns its ports with it.

fix.title: Fixing a red port
fix.text: Move or rotate the part so its port meets a matching port, or place a part that has one. Auto layout tries this for you. A part that is not connected counts for nothing, and the ship may not be allowed to fly until the problem is fixed.

rarity.title: Rarity, size and the bridge level
rarity.summary: Why some parts are stronger, why size matters, and what the bridge decides.
rarity.keywords: common uncommon rare epic legendary tier size cells grid bridge level price

rarity.title: Rarity
rarity.text: Parts come in five rarities: common, uncommon, rare, epic and legendary. Each step up is stronger and costs more. A part you already own can be upgraded to the next rarity (see Upgrading parts).

size.title: Size
size.text: Parts cover one or more cells of the grid. A bigger part gives more of its stat but uses more structure and adds weight.

bridge.title: Bridge level
bridge.text: Your bridge's rarity is your bridge level. The higher it is, the rarer the parts that appear in shops, and the better missions pay. Upgrading the bridge is the way to move up.

missions.title: Missions
missions.summary: The kinds of mission, how to know if you can take one, and how holding and expiry work.
missions.keywords: delivery transport escort mining rescue race eligible requirement hold expire reward pay cargo board

types.title: Kinds of mission
types.text: Delivery and Transport move goods or passengers. Escort protects another ship. Mining digs a material for a contract. Rescue helps a ship in trouble. Race pits you against rival ships over a route: the faster ship wins the larger share of the prize.

eligible.title: Can I take it?
eligible.text: Each mission lists what it asks of your ship, with a tick when you meet it and a cross, with your number and the number needed, when you do not. You can only accept a mission when every line is ticked. Only eligible, on by default, hides the rest.

hold.title: Hold and expiry
hold.text: Hold keeps an offer for you while you prepare. Offers expire: the countdown on the row says how long you have to start.

cargo.title: Loads and pay
cargo.text: Some deliveries need at least a number of cargo units, some load a fixed amount, and open loads fill the space you have and usually pay {{unitPay}} per unit beyond the minimum. Pay grows with distance, danger and your bridge level.

fuel.title: Fuel, repair and wear
fuel.summary: What flying costs: fuel, wear on the parts, repairs, and what happens when the tank runs dry.
fuel.keywords: fuel refuel price repair wear condition dead scrap adrift rescue sell

fuel.title: Fuel
fuel.text: Fuel costs {{fuelPrice}} per unit at a port. A trip's fuel is shown on the mission row. A ship with only ion engines burns none. If the tank runs dry the ship drifts: you can wait for a rescue or call one now, and the mission is lost. A rescue costs from {{rescueCost}}.

wear.title: Wear
wear.text: Every trip wears the parts down, more in dangerous zones and in fights. A worn part performs worse, and a part at 1% or below is dead until repaired.

repair.title: Repair
repair.text: At a port, open Repair. The price follows the part's value. Scrap helps: each scrap repairs {{pointsPerScrap}} points, up to {{scrapMax}} scrap per part. Repair takes {{hubSeconds}} seconds per point at a hub and {{outpostSeconds}} at an outpost.

sell.title: Selling
sell.text: A port buys a part for {{sellPercent}} of its value, scaled by its condition. Worn parts are worth less, so repair before you sell.

upgrading.title: Upgrading parts
upgrading.summary: How to turn a part into the next rarity without buying a new one.
upgrading.keywords: upgrade rarity money scrap crystals core fragments materials markup

rules.title: What it takes
rules.text: A part must be at 100% condition to be upgraded. You pay the price gap to the next rarity plus a markup ({{markups}}), and hand over materials.

materials.title: Materials
materials.text: Common parts need scrap. Uncommon parts need rare crystals. Rare and epic parts need core fragments as well as crystals. The amounts grow with the part's value and size.

fragments.title: Where fragments come from
fragments.text: Core fragments turn up when you scavenge in the farther zones and as rewards on missions that cross them.

work.title: Scavenging and mining
work.summary: Earning outside missions: pick through wreckage, or dig for ore.
work.keywords: scavenge scavenging mining mine ore drill foot ship cooldown find loot

scavenging.title: Scavenging
scavenging.text: At a port you can search for wreckage with the ship ({{scavengeShip}}) or on foot ({{scavengeFoot}}). You can find scrap, parts and materials; the farther zones give better finds. On foot your chances are lower. After a search you wait {{scavengeCooldown}} before the next. With the ship, pirates can find you.

mining.title: Mining
mining.text: Mining needs a mining rig installed. A free dig takes {{miningJob}} and brings back what the place gives; a mining mission asks for a named material and pays only if you bring the full amount. Richness depends on the place.

danger.title: Danger, factions and money
danger.summary: Risk, zones and pirates; who runs the places; and how credits work.
danger.keywords: risk zone pirate fight combat faction luna sun explorers pirates money credits price ally hostile

risk.title: Risk and zones
risk.text: Every place has a risk band: low, medium or high. The farther the zone, the more dangerous the trip, and the better the finds and pay. Pirates can attack on the way; fights are settled round by round from firepower, defense, mobility and luck, and you can win, escape or lose.

factions.title: Factions
factions.text: Each place is run by a faction: Luna Authority, Sun Traders, Explorers, or the pirates. Prices are better with allies and much worse in hostile hands. Your faction is your flag from the start.

money.title: Credits
money.text: You start with {{startCredits}}. Missions, scavenging and selling earn credits; parts, fuel, repair and upgrades spend them.

figures.armorCut: Hit cut per armor rating point
figures.unitPay: Open cargo, pay per extra unit
figures.markups: Upgrade markup over the price gap

tutorial.title: Getting started
tutorial.skipConfirm: Skip the tutorial for good? You can bring it back from the account menu.
tutorial.allDone: You are set. That was everything.

build.title: Build your ship
build.hint: On My Ship, press Auto layout, or place the parts yourself.
build.detail: Your ship starts as loose parts in the tray. Open My Ship and press Auto layout, or drag each part onto the grid yourself, so the ship has a bridge, an engine, a tank and the rest in place.

ports.title: Check the connections
ports.hint: Open the yard: no connection point on a part should be red. Fix any red ones (move or rotate a part), and this ticks.
ports.detail: Parts talk to each other through the small dots on their edges (ports). Green means connected, red means a wrong match. Move or turn a part until none is red, so every part is connected to the bridge.

mission.title: Take a mission
mission.hint: Open Missions and accept one your ship can take.
mission.detail: Open Missions, pick an offer your ship can take (the green Eligible tag) and press Accept. The first one is a short hop to a test pad next to your port.

dispatch.title: Dispatch it
dispatch.hint: Send the ship out and wait for the result.
dispatch.detail: Open My Ship and press Dispatch. The ship leaves the port and the mission runs by itself; the first one takes only seconds.

report.title: Read your report
report.hint: See what happened, what it paid and what the trip wore down.
report.detail: When the mission ends, open its report: what happened on the way, what it paid and what it wore down.

refuel.title: Fill the tank
refuel.hint: Your tank starts low. At the Port, open Refuel and fill it before you fly.
refuel.detail: A new ship starts with a quarter of its tank. Go to the Port, open Service, then Refuel, and buy fuel until the tank is full: a ship without fuel cannot fly.

repair.title: Repair the wear
repair.hint: At the Port, open Repair and fix what the trip wore down.
repair.detail: Flights wear parts down. At the Port open Service, then Repair, and pay to fix what is worn. If nothing is worn yet, this one comes after your first real mission.

work.title: Try other work
work.hint: At the Port: scavenge for parts or mine for ore.
work.detail: Besides missions you can earn at the Port: scavenge wreckage for parts and scrap, or mine ore if the ship has a mining rig. Open Work and start one.

hangar.title: My Ship

format.label: Choose a ship format
format.droppedWarning: {{count}} placed part outside this format will return to your available parts.
format.droppedWarning_other: {{count}} placed parts outside this format will return to your available parts.
format.required: You changed your bridge: pick a ship format for it.
format.pickHint: Pick a format to see its shape and apply it.

hangar.yardHint: Select a part, then click a cell to place it. Select a block to move, rotate or remove it.
hangar.shipRarityHint: Ship rarity — the lowest rarity among installed parts

headline.defenseHelp: What the ship can soak in a fight: the shield first, then the armor (which also cuts each hit), then the hull. Numbers are the points each layer can absorb.

energyStatus.noDrain: The ship's spare power covers it: the battery is not drained.
energyStatus.lasts: The battery lasts about {{rounds}} round(s) of this.

state.noPreview: Place at least one part to compute the sheet.

problems.NO_FUEL_CAPACITY: Chemical engine needs a fuel tank.
problems.NO_LIFE_SUPPORT: Pressurized modules but no life support installed.
problems.ENERGY_CRUISE_NEGATIVE: The systems need more power than the ship generates, so they compete for it: the bridge and life support are served first, then the ones that matter right now. Starved systems work only part of the time. Engines are not affected.
problems.BATTERY_OUTPUT_INSUFFICIENT: Weapons and shields draw more energy each round than the ship can supply (its spare power plus the batteries). In a fight some attacks and shield recovery will go unpowered — add power generation or a battery.
problems.BATTERY_CHARGE_INSUFFICIENT: Weapons and shields draw more energy than the ship's spare power plus its batteries can store — long fights will run out of power. Add power generation or a battery.
problems.EXHAUST_BLOCKED: An engine has a part directly behind its exhaust: it gives no thrust. Move it, move the part, or turn the engine.
problems.FACING_BLOCKED: A weapon has a part in its line of fire: it will not shoot. Move it or turn it.
problems.FACING_CONNECTOR: An engine or weapon has a connector on its facing side: it will not work. Turn it.
problems.SHIELD_ENERGY_LOW: If the shield is in use it can run short of energy once the battery and the ship's spare power are spent.
problems.LIFE_SUPPORT_UNPOWERED: Life support does not get enough power to run: passengers would not survive. Add power generation.
problems.HOLD_OVER_CAPACITY: The mission's cargo does not fit the ship's cargo space.
problems.NO_CARGO_HOLD: Mining keeps what it digs in the cargo hold: this ship has none. Fit a cargo hold first.
problems.HOLD_PARTS_OVER: Too many spare parts: the bridge carries only so many.
problems.PART_DISCONNECTED: A part is not connected to the bridge: fix its connectors or remove it. You can still save the layout.
problems.PORT_INCORRECT: Some connectors press against a part they do not fit (the red ports): move or rotate those parts. You can still save the layout.

errors.SHIP_ON_MISSION: The ship is on a mission.

side.storeUnavailable: The store is only available while the ship is docked.

kit.title: Your starter kit
kit.body: These are the parts your ship starts with. Nothing is installed yet: press Auto layout to assemble them, or select a part and click the grid.

rotate.blocked: There is no room to rotate this part here: move a neighbour away first.
rotate.twice: No room to turn it sideways here, so it was turned twice instead.

statHelp.class: The ship class, decided automatically by how much of the structure budget goes to cargo, pressurized (passenger) space and combat parts.
statHelp.mob: How fast the ship travels: total engine power divided by mass, times a fixed factor. More power or less mass raises it.
statHelp.crg: How much cargo the ship can carry, from every installed cargo hold.
statHelp.min: How much ore the ship can mine per trip, from every installed mining rig.
statHelp.hp: Total hit points from every installed part. Lost in combat, restored by repair.
statHelp.pot: Total thrust from every installed engine. Feeds mobility.
statHelp.pdf: Combat damage output from every installed weapon.
statHelp.bli: Armor sits behind the shield. It cuts every hit that gets past the shield by a flat amount (see the number in brackets), then its pool soaks the rest, and only what is left reaches the hull. It wears down in a fight, and a worn armor cuts less. Hull parts give hit points, not armor.
statHelp.esc: A pool of damage soaked FIRST: it takes as much of every hit as it can hold. It recovers its own points every combat round, and each point it recovers costs combat energy — no energy, no recovery.
statHelp.sen: Spots ambushes early, lowering the chance of being surprised in an encounter.
statHelp.mass: Total weight of every installed part (plus a loaded tank's fuel, where that adds weight). Pulls mobility down.
statHelp.fuelCap: How much fuel the ship can hold, from every installed tank.
statHelp.fuelUse: How much fuel is burned per unit of travel.
statHelp.energyCont: Cruising power balance: what generators produce minus what always draws power (sensors, life support, mining rigs...). Below zero the ship still flies, but its engines only get the share of power that exists. Separate from combat power, which comes from the batteries.
statHelp.energyCombat: Energy that weapons and shields draw each combat round (always zero or negative). The ship's own spare power (cruising power above zero) pays for it first; the batteries cover only what that cannot. Pick the batteries-only mode to keep the ship's spare power out of combat.
statHelp.batCharge: Total energy the batteries can hold for combat. It only needs to cover what the ship's own spare power cannot — with enough generation you need no battery at all.
statHelp.batOutput: The most energy the batteries can deliver in one round. It only needs to cover what the ship's own spare power cannot pay for each round.
statHelp.batInput: How fast the battery recharges between fights.
statHelp.autonomy: How far a full tank takes the ship, in route-distance units (the same units as route lengths). Below it: how many of the world's routes that covers.
statHelp.condition: Average wear across every installed part, from 100% (new) down.
statHelp.structure: How much of the structure budget the bridge sets is used by everything else installed.

placement.exhaust: Parts are behind this engine's exhaust — turn it or move it to the back edge of the ship.
placement.facing: Parts are in this weapon's line of fire — turn it or move it to the edge of the ship.

warnings.title: Warnings
warnings.explain: The ship can fly, but weaker — fix these to get its full performance.

clear.title: Empty the ship?
clear.body: All {{count}} installed parts go back to the inventory. Nothing is sold or lost, but the ship cannot fly until it is assembled again.

hold.line: Carried: {{parts}} of {{slots}} spare-part slots. Your goods (ore, scrap) are kept ashore and take no space.
hold.partsOver: Too many spare parts to depart: sell or leave some.
hold.hint: Spare parts ride free in the bridge slots (one slot per part, any size or rarity). Only the cargo a mission loads takes cargo space.

admin.title: Admin
admin.adjustmentsNote: Manual support adjustments are excluded from entering / leaving / net.
admin.name: Name

warnings.grant: Adds credits to the player's wallet. Recorded in the audit log.
warnings.remove: Removes credits from the wallet (cannot go below zero).
warnings.clear: Sets a negative balance back to zero.
warnings.password: Sets a new password for this account and signs it out everywhere. The password itself is never recorded in the audit log.
warnings.unstick: Expires the ship's active mission and parks the ship in port. Its future route presence is deleted.
warnings.ban: Suspends the account at once and ends all sessions. Admin accounts cannot be banned.
warnings.reset: Wipes parts, materials, repairs, missions and sessions, returns the ship to the home port and re-applies the starter kit and credits. History is kept. This cannot be undone.
warnings.fastOps: Per player: this player's missions, trips, scavenging, mining and repairs finish in a few seconds (admin.debug_fast_ops_seconds) while the UI still shows the real durations. Takes effect on the next job started.

admin.mismatch: Replay DIVERGES from the stored log

dialogue.title: Dialogue scenes
dialogue.help: What the mentor says to the pilot, scene by scene. A scene starts when its trigger holds (once per pilot) and scenes are offered in order. Each node is one popup; choices can branch or take the pilot somewhere.

triggers.low_fuel: The tank runs low after a flight

givers.linesHelp: Short lines the giver says, one list per key. An empty pool means the template text is used. {destination}, {cargo} and {reward} are filled in from the offer.
givers.emptyPool: No lines yet — the template description is used.
givers.personalityHelp: What this giver offers: relative weights per mission type (0 = never), the zone band they hand out, and the tone used to pick their lines.

connectorRules.notConfigured: Not configured: parts of this type get universal connectors until rules are set.
connectorRules.weightHelp: Relative weights per side (0 = never). One kind is rolled per side when a part is generated; the result never changes afterwards. Engines/weapons: side W must stay none.
connectorRules.forbidden: Forbidden combinations (a roll matching every chosen side is rejected)
connectorRules.oneKindPerPart: One kind per part (all connected sides use the same kind, ports at the same place on every side)
connectorRules.diagram: Connector kinds allowed on each side
connectorRules.noPortHelp: To make a side sometimes bare, allow the dash (none) on it and give it a weight: 1 against 3 for central means a 25% chance of no port on that side. At least the minimum number of sides always keeps a port.

parts.partType: The part's permanent code (used by saves and the catalog). Lowercase with underscores; it cannot be changed after creation.
parts.displayName: What players see in menus, the market and reports, in both languages.
parts.description: The short blurb on the part's card and popup, in both languages.
parts.partClass: What the part does for the ship. Bridge is required, engines move it, weapons/defense fight, cargo carries, and so on. Engines and weapons also have a facing (see connector rules).
parts.rarity: How rare the part is: sets its colour, how often it appears in shops and drops, and which ship formats it can unlock.
parts.mass: Weight in tonnes. Heavier ships are slower (mobility = thrust ÷ mass).
parts.structureCost: How much of the ship's structure budget this part uses. Bridges use a negative number: they PROVIDE the budget.
parts.basePrice: The shop price of a brand-new part in credits, before location and condition adjustments.
parts.scrapValue: What the part is worth as scrap when it is broken beyond use.
parts.partHp: Hit points of this part itself, used when parts take damage.
parts.pot: Potential output: engine thrust. Divided by the ship's total mass it gives mobility.
parts.pdf: Point defense fire: the part's firepower in combat.
parts.bli: Build integrity: armor that cuts damage taken.
parts.esc: Escape/shield rating: absorbs damage before it reaches the armor and hull.
parts.sen: Sensor rating: how well the ship detects ambushes and enemies.
parts.min: Mining output: needed for mining missions and jobs.
parts.energyCont: Continuous energy: positive generates power, negative draws it all the time. The ship's total must stay at or above zero to fly.
parts.energyCombat: Energy drawn per combat round by this part (negative) — batteries must cover it.
parts.fuelCap: Fuel tank capacity this part adds.
parts.fuelUse: Fuel an engine burns per 100 distance (empty for parts that do not burn fuel; ion engines use 0).
parts.batCharge: How much energy this battery stores for combat.
parts.batOutput: How much energy this battery can deliver each combat round.
parts.specialProp: Special abilities the part grants (passenger space, life support).
parts.connectorRules: How the ports of a NEW part of this type are generated. The result is fixed on the part forever; changing the rules only affects parts made afterwards.

materials.displayName: Name shown to players, both languages.
materials.rarity: How rare the ore is: drives how hard it is to find when mining.
materials.basePrice: What the material sells for at a typical port (before location and mood).

factions.id: The faction's permanent code. Art files and missions are tied to it.
factions.displayName: Name shown to players, both languages.
factions.description: The faction's pitch on the selection screen, both languages.
factions.color: The faction colour (hex, like #4a90d9) used on badges and the map.
factions.playable: Whether new players can choose this faction at the start. Off for NPC factions such as pirates.
factions.relations: How this faction treats each other faction. Hostile ones attack on sight; allies leave you alone; it also changes prices there.
factions.starterKitHint: Optional starter-kit suggestion for the faction (leave empty unless you know the format).

locations.id: The place's permanent code. Art files are tied to it.
locations.displayName: Name shown to players, both languages.
locations.description: Short description of the place, both languages.
locations.type: What kind of place it is (port, shipyard, outpost…). Mission templates use it to decide where they can be offered.
locations.zone: Danger zone of the place (0 = safe core, higher = more dangerous). Routes take the riskier end.
locations.factionId: The faction that controls the place: sets prices and how you are treated.
locations.isolation: Price multiplier for being remote (fuel, repairs, parts): 1 = normal, above 1 = more expensive.
locations.mood: Local price mood: below 1 is cheaper, above 1 is dearer.
locations.services: What the player can do here: buy parts, sell, repair, take missions, passengers.

routes.nodeBId: The other end (the pair must be unique and ordered).
routes.distance: Length of the route: sets travel time and fuel burned.
routes.danger: How dangerous the route is: raises encounter chances and rewards.

environments.displayName: Name shown to players, both languages.
environments.description: What this environment is like, both languages.
environments.level: Hazard level: how much wear the environment causes on a leg.
environments.fuelMult: Multiplier on fuel burned while flying through it.
environments.subsystemTarget: Which ship subsystem this environment strains.
environments.mitigatingPart: A part type that protects against it.

mission-templates.displayName: Mission title shown on the board, both languages.
mission-templates.description: The brief shown on the board, both languages.
mission-templates.type: What kind of mission it is. Each type has its own rules for requirements, encounters and pay (Race: compete against rival ships for a prize by finishing place).
mission-templates.factionId: The faction that offers this mission.
mission-templates.requirements: Where the mission can be offered: allowed location types and factions, plus optional ship needs.
mission-templates.rewardCalc: Extra reward parameters (leave empty for the standard formula).
mission-templates.deadlineCalc: Extra deadline parameters (leave empty for the standard rules).
mission-templates.encounterPolicy: How encounters during this mission behave.

drop-tables.source: What activity rolls on this table (for example scavenging).
drop-tables.tiers: The chance of each rarity tier turning up. Chances must add up to 100%.

ship-formats.displayName: Name shown to players, both languages.
ship-formats.cells: The buildable cells of the ship's yard. The bridge sits at the starred cell.
ship-formats.cellTarget: A soft target for the number of cells: shown while drawing, never enforced.
ship-formats.minRarity: The lowest bridge rarity that unlocks this format.

structured.noParams: No extra parameters — the standard formula is used.

services.sellHelp: Players can sell parts and materials here.
services.repairHelp: The repair shop is open here.
services.missionsHelp: The mission board lists offers from here.
services.passengersHelp: Transport and passenger jobs start here.
services.refuelHelp: The fuel dock is open here (a missing flag counts as open).
services.upgradeHelp: Parts can be upgraded here (a missing flag counts as open).

special.pressurizedHelp: Counts as passenger space (needed for transport missions).
special.lifeSupportHelp: Keeps passengers alive (needed together with a cabin).

policy.missionForcesFleeHelp: The ship runs from every encounter on this mission instead of fighting.

requirements.originTypes: Offered at these kinds of places
requirements.originFactions: Offered by places of these factions
requirements.cargoHelp: Minimum cargo capacity the ship needs.
requirements.minMobilityHelp: Minimum mobility to enter a race (default: the Race config).
requirements.destinationTypes: Ends at these kinds of places

scav.what: Search the wreckage around {{place}} for parts other pilots left behind. It is manual work at the place: the ship stays in port but is busy meanwhile, and a report tells you what was found.

scav.risk: The riskier the place (zone {{zone}}), the better and rarer the finds — and pirates may find you while you search. Rare parts only turn up in dangerous places.
scav.quality: Everything you find is USED: about {{min}}–{{max}}% condition at this place. Repair it, install it or sell it.
scav.finds: At {{place}} a search can turn up one or more parts; a pirate-held field gives the most.
scav.scrap: Wreckage here also holds scrap: worn-out remains that sell at a fixed price at any port.
scav.where: Only where your ship is docked; each place has its own waiting time between jobs.
scav.title: Scavenge the wreckage
scav.nothing: About {{percent}}% of searches here find nothing (the safer the place, the more often).
scav.handicap: Your ship cannot fly right now. Scavenging does not need flight, but you search at a disadvantage: only {{percent}}% of the usual chance to find anything.
scav.noShip: Your ship cannot fly — no usable bridge, engine or connected parts. Search on foot instead: it needs no ship.
scav.shipRepairing: Your ship is under repair and cannot sail meanwhile. Search on foot instead: it needs no ship.
scav.riskFoot: The riskier the place (zone {{zone}}), the better and rarer the finds. On foot nothing can attack you. Rare parts only turn up in dangerous places.

ship.name: With the ship

scav.footNotice: On foot you only get {{percent}}% of the usual chance to find anything. In return, nothing attacks you and the ship takes no damage.

rescue.title: Floating in space
rescue.body: Your ship ran out of fuel and drifts where it stopped. Nothing can be done with it until it is towed to a base. Pick how: wait for the rescue to arrive (cheaper) or call it now. Either may leave your balance negative.
rescue.waiting: Rescue on its way — arrives in
rescue.confirmWait: Wait for the rescue? It arrives in about {{minutes}} minutes and tows the ship to {{base}}. You pay {{cost}} ¢ when it arrives.
rescue.confirmNow: Call the rescue now? The ship is towed to {{base}} at once and you pay {{cost}} ¢.
rescue.waitStarted: The rescue is on its way. You pay when it arrives.
rescue.done: Towed to port for {{cost}} ¢. Fuel on board: {{fuel}}.

role.BRIDGE: Required. Every ship needs exactly one: it is the command core, keeps the pilot alive if the ship is destroyed, and sets how much structure the ship can carry.
role.ENGINE: Required: a ship with no engine cannot move. Chemical engines also need a fuel tank; ion engines need steady power instead.
role.TANK: Holds the fuel. Any ship with a chemical engine needs at least one, and a bigger tank means longer trips between refuels.
role.BATTERY: Stores energy for combat. Weapons and shields draw from it, so it must cover their demand or the ship is not allowed to fly.
role.REACTOR: Generates energy continuously. Engines and systems draw power all the time, so total generation must cover them.
role.WEAPON: Adds firepower. Needed for escort missions and to win fights; costs energy in combat.
role.DEFENSE: Adds armor, shield and hit points so the ship survives attacks. It adds no speed, cargo or firepower, and its mass slows you down.
role.CARGO: Adds cargo capacity. More cargo means bigger deliveries and better pay, but adds mass.
role.SENSOR: Spots trouble early, which lowers the chance of being ambushed on a route.
role.UTILITY: Special equipment that unlocks certain missions (mining rigs, life support, and so on).

flag.pressurized: Passenger module: a ship carrying one needs a life support part.

engineTuning.title: Engine tuning
engineTuning.intro: Run the engines at their listed power, or push them for speed. Pushing risks an engine failure on each leg. The battery management is set here too.
engineTuning.locked: The engines can only be tuned while the ship is in port.

hint.chem: Always at least 100%. Above 1: faster, burns much more fuel, wears the chemical engines and can overheat.
hint.ion: Burns no fuel but draws power, and the draw climbs faster than the thrust. Above 1: more thrust, wears the ion engines AND the batteries, and can overheat.

engineTuning.power: Power: makes {{supply}}, uses {{demand}}, spare {{spare}} (a shortfall starves other systems; engines keep running).
engineTuning.clean: {{percent}}% chance no engine fails on the whole trip.

engineTuning.tripFuel: Fuel: needs {{needed}}, you carry {{have}} (at the listed levels: {{base}}).
engineTuning.tripNoFit: At these levels the trip needs more fuel than the ship carries. Throttle the chemical engines down, or push the ion engines if the power allows.
engineTuning.thrustLine: {{group}}: {{value}} of the speed ({{percent}}% of the thrust; listed: {{base}})
engineTuning.wear: Wear per leg from the push alone: chemical engines −{{chem}}, ion engines −{{ion}}, batteries −{{battery}}.

battery.label: Battery management
battery.hint: Where the combat energy comes from: the batteries only, everything the ship makes, or an override that drives the systems harder.

landing.kicker: A space logistics and ship-building strategy game
landing.title: Rust and Spark
landing.pitch: Build your ship from parts, plan the run, send it out on a real-time clock, and read what happened. A shared world of pilots, factions and a living economy.

build.title: Build
build.text: Assemble a ship from parts in five rarities and several sizes. Every part has weight, power and a place on the grid.

plan.title: Plan
plan.text: Tune the engines and the battery, load your cargo, pick a mission and a route. Fuel, danger and time decide what pays.

fly.title: Fly
fly.text: Missions run on the server in real time. Come back when you like: the clock keeps going without you.

read.title: Read
read.text: Every run is told like a text RPG: fights, wear, loot and what it cost. Repair, upgrade and go again.

more.title: Not a game you can just leave running

missions.title: Many ways to earn
missions.text: Deliveries, passengers, mining, scavenging, escorts and races. Open cargo pays by the unit; fixed loads fill your hold.

economy.title: A living economy
economy.text: Upgrades need money plus scrap, crystals and rare cores found in dangerous places. Ore you dig up is yours to sell.

risk.title: Everything costs
risk.text: Pirates, wear and running dry. A tow costs credits and the mission. Spare parts and cargo compete for space.

factions.title: Four powers, one sector
factions.intro: Each faction runs its own ports, contracts and prices, and none of them likes the others the same way.

cta.title: Ready to fly?
cta.text: Create a pilot, pick a faction and take your first job.
